artist.name: Lang Jingshan
artist.bio: Lang Jingshan, also romanized as Long Chin-san and Lang Ching-shan, was a pioneering photographer and one of the first Chinese photojournalists. He has been called "indisputably the most prominent figure in the history of Chinese art photography", and the "Father of Asian Photography". He joined the Royal Photographic Society in 1937 and gained his Associateship in 1940 and Fellowship in 1942. and in 1980, the Photographic Society of America named him one of the world's top ten master photographers. He was the first Chinese photographer to take artistic nude shots, and was also known for the unique "composite photography" technique he created.

summary:
Australian culture and community resilience took centre stage this week, highlighted by The Avalanches’ return with a nostalgic album and a community-led film project in K’gari exploring the history of local brumbies in World War I. In sports, the Bathurst 1000 buzzed with excitement as rookie Zach Bates secured pole position, while cricket fans celebrated Australian players outperforming Sir Donald Bradman’s records during the first Test against South Africa. These stories reflect a vibrant national identity grounded in creativity, historical reflection, and sporting excellence.

Internationally, scientific progress and humanitarian solidarity offered grounds for hope. Researchers traced the cell-by-cell development of a mouse embryo using gene-editing technologies, while a new cancer drug, daraxonrasib, was reported to double survival rates for patients with advanced disease. In the realm of exploration, scientists studying Chang’e-6 lunar soil discovered a previously unknown magnetic mineral, γ-Fe, expanding our understanding of the Moon. Meanwhile, global humanitarian communities were honoured for their lifesaving aid, emphasizing the enduring spirit of care and resilience in the face of crisis.

In Australia, the government’s firm stance against importing Russian fuel underscored a commitment to ethical energy choices, while a study on disaster resilience highlighted the importance of 'interspecies relational solidarity' in caring for animals during climate events. These constructive responses, from policy to community care, demonstrate a nation focused on integrity, environmental stewardship, and the well-being of all members of the community.
